questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure role-based access control
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Azure RBAC: an authorization system that controls who can perform which actions on Azure resources and at what scope.
Role definition: using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications.
Azure RBAC: the level at which a role assignment applies, such as management group, subscription, resource group, or resource.
Security principal: a role assignment at a higher scope applying to child resources.
Security principal: the user, group, service principal, or managed identity receiving a role assignment.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Azure RBAC — an authorization system that controls who can perform which actions on Azure resources and at what scope; and Security principal — the user, group, service principal, or managed identity receiving a role assignment.

questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure role-based access control
questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately reflect the concepts covered in this unit?

options.text: Role definition: a collection of permitted management actions such as read, write, or delete operations.
Scope: the level at which a role assignment applies, such as management group, subscription, resource group, or resource.
Scope: verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.
Role definition: granting only the permissions needed to perform required tasks.
Scope: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Role definition — a collection of permitted management actions such as read, write, or delete operations; and Scope — the level at which a role assignment applies, such as management group, subscription, resource group, or resource.
